summary: We identify five Earth micro-sites that analog lunar and Martian base locations: Marmul (Dhofar, Oman), Beacon Valley (Antarctica), Haughton Crater central uplift (Canada), Lava Beds cave zone (USA) and Geldingadalir lava field (Reykjanes, Iceland). Each site is chosen for specific terrain, geology, environment and resource traits, and is matched to Moon and Mars targets using NASA open data.
details: Our project proposes five Earth micro-sites (coordinates given in the demo) as analogs for lunar and Martian bases, covering a Mars sedimentary desert (Dhofar), Mars-like ground ice (Beacon Valley), a lunar-like impact crater interior (Haughton), lava-tube shelters (Lava Beds) and fresh basalt (Reykjanes). Method: we compare the same layers across Moon, Mars and Earth: topography (LOLA, MOLA, SRTM), geology and mineralogy (LROC, HiRISE, ASTER) and environment (Landsat, Worldview), browsed through NASA Moon Trek, Mars Trek and Earthdata. The output is a repeatable comparison model with a scored analog profile per site, usable for Artemis and Mars mission planning. Tools: NASA open data portals only (Moon Trek, Mars Trek, LROC, HiRISE, PDS, Earthdata, Worldview), plus public literature on the AMADEE-18 Dhofar mission. Coordinates are approximate and should be refined in the Trek tools.
projectRefs: AMADEE-18 Mars analog mission (Austrian Space Forum)
